title: Rabbi Joey Soffer: Mesilat Yesharim class #18

chapters.title: The definition of separation and stature
Why there was no enactment against pleasures
Story regarding handing someone over to the government
Avoiding bodily harm and false asceticism

summary: Rabbi Soffer continues the study of Mesilat Yesharim, discussing the path of perishut, separating from excess worldly pleasures and unnecessary enjoyments while maintaining one's proper stature. He explains the balance between necessary consumption and excessive desire, noting that while extreme stringencies are not mandated for the general public, they are undertaken by pious individuals for spiritual elevation. The class also covers applying stringencies in halakhic matters without letting them lead to other spiritual failings.
questions: What is the proper approach to taking vacations and leisure time according to Mesilat Yesharim?
Why didn't the Hakhamim enact a universal fence against all worldly pleasures?
How does one determine whether an item or enjoyment is considered a necessary need versus excess?
What is the rule regarding taking on stringencies in Halakha without causing a negative outcome?
